correctness.rationale: For every k>=2,a<b and ak<n<bk, coordinatewise minima of the two periodic feasible lifts preserve every gap inequality. The active-coordinate dependency digraph has no directed cycle: a two-cycle would impose a=b on a gap, and a full directed circuit would force n=ak or n=bk. A legal decrement thus exists until the meet is attained; the reverse descent from the target yields a path with length exactly the L1 transportation sum. Cyclic order cannot change in legal slides, establishing matching lower bound. Exhaustive BFS and independent constructive checks passed over the stated finite ranges; they supplement the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly solves a natural constrained optimal-motion problem on every discrete cycle with simultaneous hard minimum/maximum spacing. It identifies a surprisingly zero-detour regime and gives an explicit quadratic-time distance formula plus feasible geodesic construction, not just a count or a small-instance property. The minimum-independent-domination specialization supplies a directly motivated nontrivial infinite-family application; boundary rigidity explains why strict interior conditions matter.
